The deterministic readiness status is 'fatigued,' and the recovery capability label is 'I only have training data,' suggesting that the athlete's recent recovery signals are limited and do not provide a clear picture of their true state. Given this context, the primary goal is to sustain high training quality while building race-relevant durability, but the current state necessitates a cautious approach to ensure proper recovery and prevent further fatigue accumulation.
Ensure adequate rest and recovery on the rest day. Avoid any structured training on this day to allow the body to fully recover.
Monitor heart rate variability (HRV) and resting heart rate (RHR) closely. Aim for a gradual increase in these metrics over the next few days to signal improved recovery.

Consider incorporating some form of active recovery on the rest day, such as a short walk or easy yoga session, to aid in recovery without completely breaking the routine.
